Found by the specled_-dn4.9 audit (2026-07-26T00:25:30Z, ruling N2 — the removal itself was chartered, but the asymmetry it leaves is worth resolving).

dn4.9 item 4 removed 'state.modules || state.modules_fn.()' from flush/1, so flush now raises where it previously recovered. The neighbouring record_inventory/2 still carries its own %{modules: nil} recovery clause. Unreachable under ExUnit's real lifecycle, but one sibling defending against a state the other no longer defends against is a latent trap for the next reader.

Fix: pick one — restore the fallback in flush/1, drop the sibling clause in record_inventory/2, or comment why they legitimately differ.

## ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT (specled_-i4x)

Advances: (none — internal defensive-code hygiene, no spec subject)

BLOCKED BY specled_-dn4.12 — edge CONFIRMED against the actual diff. dn4.12 does not relocate
flush/1 itself; it deletes 27 lines IMMEDIATELY ABOVE it (source_file/1, source_to_binary/1,
repo_relative_path/1 at formatter.ex:260-286) and replaces them with one delegating line.
`defp repo_relative_path(_), do: nil` at :286 is TWO LINES above flush/1 at :288, so a 3-line
git context hunk for your second edit point includes the exact line dn4.12 deletes. Parallel
work conflicts. AFTER dn4.12 lands, flush/1 sits at ~:262 and your target line at ~:263 —
re-locate before editing, do not trust the line numbers below.

Allowed touches: lib/specled_ex/coverage/formatter.ex ONLY.

PREFERRED END STATE (auditor-recommended; removes untested dead code):
- Delete formatter.ex:201-213 — the %{modules: nil} clause of record_inventory/2 AND its
  two-line comment at :201-202. The comment MUST go with the clause; leaving it behind is a
  false claim about the code, which is exactly the class this sweep exists to remove.
- Add one comment above the surviving `defp record_inventory(%ExUnit.Test{} = test, state)`
  (:215) stating the shared invariant: :modules/:file_map are populated once at suite_started;
  both this clause and flush/1 assume that event arrived. ExUnit always emits it before any
  test_finished/suite_finished.
- Add the same one-line pointer at `modules = state.modules` (formatter.ex:289 at the epic
  base, ~:263 after dn4.12).

Out of Scope (files):
- .spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md — no requirement constrains this.
  specled.coverage_capture.formatter_auditor and .unhooked_degrade are both SILENT on
  module-scope resolution when suite_started never fired.
- .spec/realization_hashes.json, CHANGELOG.md, VERSION, everything else.

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do NOT add a test. A test driving test_finished without suite_started pins a state ExUnit
  cannot produce.
- If ALTERNATIVE A is chosen instead (restore `state.modules || state.modules_fn.()`), it
  reverts dn4.9 ruling N2 and REQUIRES a regression test in
  test/specled_ex/coverage/formatter_test.exs; record the reversal in the commit message.

Verification:

  mix format --check-formatted
  mix spec.check --no-run-commands
Realization hash: zero risk. Both flush/1 and record_inventory/2 are defp;
"SpecLedEx.Coverage.Formatter" (.spec/realization_hashes.json:273) is head-union hashed over
public exports only.

Expected diff: 1 file, ~+3/-13.

VERDICT: still_applicable   EFFORT: trivial

== SCOPED REMAINING WORK ==
Resolve the asymmetry in /Users/mz/src/specled_ex-self-identifying-descriptors/lib/specled_ex/coverage/formatter.ex. Pick ONE end state:

PREFERRED (cheapest, matches the auditor invariant the moduledoc already asserts, and removes untested dead code):
- Delete formatter.ex:201-212 entirely — both the `%{modules: nil}` clause of `record_inventory/2` AND its two-line comment ("A `test_finished` arriving with no prior `suite_started` resolves module scope lazily rather than crashing"). The comment MUST go with the clause; leaving it would be a false claim about the code, which is precisely the class the td7 branch is sweeping.
- Replace it with one comment above the surviving `defp record_inventory(%ExUnit.Test{} = test, state)` (currently formatter.ex:214) stating the shared invariant, e.g.: "`:modules`/`:file_map` are populated once at `suite_started`; both this clause and `flush/1` assume that event arrived. ExUnit always emits it before any `test_finished`/`suite_finished`."
- Add the same one-line pointer at formatter.ex:289 (`modules = state.modules`) so the next reader sees why there is no fallback.
- No test change required (nothing exercises the deleted clause), and no new test is warranted — a test that drives `test_finished` without `suite_started` would pin a state ExUnit cannot produce.

ALTERNATIVE A (restore symmetry the other way): change formatter.ex:289 back to `modules = state.modules || state.modules_fn.()`. If this is chosen, it needs a regression test in test/specled_ex/coverage/formatter_test.exs asserting `{:suite_finished, %{}}` on a post-`Formatter.init/1` state (never `suite_started`) writes/refuses cleanly instead of raising — otherwise the restored branch is dead code again and dn4.9's removal ruling is simply reverted without cause.

ALTERNATIVE B (document the difference): add a comment at formatter.ex:288-289 explaining why flush legitimately assumes `state.modules` while its sibling does not. Weakest option — there is no such legitimate reason on record; both are unreachable under ExUnit's real lifecycle.

Do NOT touch .spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md: no requirement constrains this. `specled.coverage_capture.formatter_auditor` (coverage_capture.spec.md:593-611) and `specled.coverage_capture.unhooked_degrade` (:613-626) are both silent on module-scope resolution when `suite_started` never fired.

== EXPECTED TOUCHES ==
lib/specled_ex/coverage/formatter.ex

== RISK NOTES ==
REALIZATION HASH: no risk. Both `flush/1` and `record_inventory/2` are `defp`. The api_boundary binding for this module is the bare-module entry "SpecLedEx.Coverage.Formatter" (.spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md:124), hashed by SpecLedEx.Realization.Canonical.hash_module_head_union/2 (lib/specled_ex/realization/canonical.ex:176-187) over `discover_module_exports/2` — public exports' heads only, so private-function edits cannot move it. The implementation-tier binding is "SpecLedEx.Coverage.Formatter.init/1" (coverage_capture.spec.md:145), untouched by this work; and .spec/realization_hashes.json contains only the `api_boundary` top-level key, so no implementation-tier hash is pinned at all.

SPEC REQUIREMENT IDS: none touched. This ticket carries no spec subject and needs no .spec/ edit, so it does not collide with specled_-npo (which edits the `envelope_meta` requirement in the same spec file) or specled_-ako.

FILE CONFLICT: specled_-dn4.12 is the only other ticket in the set that edits lib/specled_ex/coverage/formatter.ex. Its region is immediately adjacent — it removes/relocates `source_to_binary/1` (formatter.ex:274-276) and `repo_relative_path/1` (formatter.ex:277-286), directly above `flush/1` at :288, and per its comments may hoist them plus `source_file/1` into a new shared home (verifier suggested `SpecLedEx.Coverage.Paths`). Line-level git conflict is unlikely (zd8's regions are :201-212 and :289) but a structural relocation of formatter.ex would rebase over it. ORDERING: land specled_-dn4.12 FIRST, then apply zd8 on top; zd8 is a 3-line diff and trivially re-derived, dn4.12 is not.

NO DEPENDENCY otherwise: zd8 is self-contained and does not block or require anything else in the set.

GATE: touching only private functions and comments, `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` are the only relevant gates; the PREFERRED option deletes an unreachable clause so no test can regress. If ALTERNATIVE A is chosen instead, note it re-introduces the exact line dn4.9 ruling N2 chartered for removal — that reversal should be recorded in the commit message.

Mechanical checks:
- Files touched: 1 (lib/specled_ex/coverage/formatter.ex) — 1 commit, 0352156e, +2/-13
- Files outside Allowed globs: 0
- .spec/** untouched: confirmed. `git diff --name-only 06860c75..HEAD -- '.spec/**' CHANGELOG.md VERSION` returns zero paths;

- realization_hashes.json diff: empty, and expected rather than merely observed. The file has exactly one

Semantic checks:
- Deleted clause was unreachable — BOTH halves verified independently:
  (a) No test drives it. The only entry point to record_inventory/2 is `handle_cast({:test_finished, ...})`
      (formatter.ex:178-180); it is called nowhere else in lib/ or test/. Every `{:test_finished, ...}` cast
      against this formatter in the suite is preceded by suite_started: formatter_test.exs:219 (after :209),
      :245 (after :240), :262 (after :256), :329 (after :325), :769/:770 (after :763). The one remaining case,
      formatter_test.exs:109, casts against `:disabled`, which short-circuits at formatter.ex:161 before
      record_inventory is ever reached. test/specled_ex/tagged_tests/formatter_test.exs drives a DIFFERENT module
      (SpecLedEx.TaggedTests.Formatter) and never touches this code. So with `modules: nil` (set only by
      run_init/1, formatter.ex:151-158) no test ever reaches the deleted clause.
  (b) ExUnit cannot produce the state. Established in ExUnit's own runner:
      /Users/mz/.asdf/installs/elixir/1.18.1-otp-27/lib/ex_unit/lib/ex_unit/runner.ex — `run_with_trap/2` calls
      `configure/4` at :40 (which registers all formatters via `EM.add_handler`, see `defp configure` :
      "Enum.each(opts[:formatters], &EM.add_handler(manager, &1, opts))"), then `EM.suite_started` at :44, and only
      THEN `async_loop/4` at :49, which is where every `EM.test_finished` (:239, :262, :400, :404) originates;
      `EM.suite_finished` follows at :62. Handlers are therefore attached before suite_started, and suite_started
      is emitted before any test_finished/suite_finished. The specled side matches: Mix.Tasks.Spec.Cover.Test
      calls `install_formatter/0` (spec.cover.test.ex:258-269, via `ExUnit.configure(formatters: ...)`) at
      spec.cover.test.ex:219, before the suite runs — there is no mid-run handler attach that could miss
      suite_started.
- Comment deleted WITH its clause, not orphaned: confirmed. The diff removes formatter.ex:201-213 as one hunk —
  both lines of "# Inventory only — no per-test snapshot. A `test_finished` arriving with no / # prior
  `suite_started` resolves module scope lazily rather than crashing." are gone along with the clause body. Grepped
  lib/specled_ex/coverage/ for surviving "lazy"/"lazily" prose: zero hits. (The three "lazy-capture" hits in
  .spec/specs/coverage_capture.spec.md:544/625/958 are about unhooked-test payloads, a different mechanism, and
  they assert the fallback does NOT exist — unaffected.)
- New comments are factually true — claim by claim:
  * ":modules/:file_map are populated at suite_started" — TRUE. handle_cast({:suite_started, _}) at
    formatter.ex:164-175 does Map.put(:modules, modules) and Map.put(:file_map, build_file_map(modules));
    run_init/1 (:151-158) is the only other writer and sets them to nil/%{}. Nothing else recomputes them.
  * "flush/1 assumes it" — TRUE. flush/1 reads state.modules at :252 (feeding snapshot_fn) and state.file_map at
    :271, :284 and :292, with no nil guard anywhere.
  * "ExUnit emits suite_started first" — TRUE, per runner.ex:40/44/49/62 above.
  * The deletion also RETIRES a pre-existing inaccuracy: the moduledoc at formatter.ex:88-90 says :modules_fn is
    "called once, at `suite_started`" — the deleted clause was the one path that could call it a second time.
  See Notes for one wording imprecision in the same sentence.
- No behavior change for reachable inputs: confirmed. The surviving record_inventory/2 clause and flush/1 bodies

- Targeted verification (all from the stage worktree /Users/mz/src/specled_ex-formatter-defensive-symmetry):

Verdict: PASS

Notes (advisory only, no Gap):
1. The added sentence is byte-identical at both sites, and its deictic "this clause" does not resolve cleanly at
   either. Above record_inventory/2 (formatter.ex:201) it says the clause assumes the ":modules/:file_map setup"
   — but that clause reads neither field; it only touches state.table and state.degraded_async?. The invariant the
   sentence asserts is true of the module; the attribution to that specific clause is not. Inside flush/1
   (formatter.ex:251) "this clause and `flush/1`" is self-referential — "this clause" IS flush/1, and there is no
   sibling clause at that site. Not graded a Gap: the asserted invariant (suite_started populates both fields, is
   emitted first, and flush/1 depends on it) is accurate, the wording is verbatim what the contract prescribed, and
   no reader can derive a wrong belief about runtime behavior from it. A one-line re-point would be strictly
   better, e.g. above record_inventory/2: "ExUnit emits `suite_started` before any `test_finished`; this clause no
   longer recovers when it did not — see `flush/1`, which reads the `:modules`/`:file_map` it sets." and inside
   flush/1: "`:modules`/`:file_map` come from `suite_started`, which ExUnit always emits first — no fallback."
2. The deleted comment's first sentence ("Inventory only — no per-test snapshot.") described the surviving clause,

3. Line 201 is 108 chars — longer than most comments in this file, but `mix format --check-formatted` passes and

- No test drives it: record_inventory/2's only entry point is handle_cast({:test_finished, ...}),

The realization-baseline claim was likewise proven rather than inferred: both edited functions are
defp, and the two Formatter entries are a bare-module head-union over PUBLIC exports plus an
untouched init/1, so private-function edits cannot move either. Confirmed by an actual
realization-drift run, not just by an empty diff.

The comment went with its clause, which is the point of this ticket's class: an orphaned comment
describing removed behavior would have made the ticket self-defeating, since it is part of a sweep
to eliminate exactly that.
